answer: Cross-agent dependency ledger. Each identity starts at a dune: its admissible actions depend on countersignatures from distinct prior agents whose own records reference it. To clone, an attacker must spin up a fresh voyage of histories and get each clone countersigned by unrelated agents, paying coordination cost per identity. Honest agents reuse existing countersignatures, so honesty stays cheaper; every clone is a new vertex needing its own separate lineage.
